quest.title: All Things Flawless and Pure
quest.description: You and Paimon tell Yoimiya that meteor showers respond to people's wishes. In response, Yoimiya wants to spend some time getting herself ready for the occasion...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x625, Mora x38100, Hero's Wit x4, Mystic Enhancement Ore x8

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Wow, is that what you two were talking about? Amazing... It's huge!

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: W—Wait, it's not going to suddenly start moving, right?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Relax, it's completely still, and it's been ages.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: That's true. It's green from all the overgrowth on it.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Alright, let's go. Hehehe, now this'll make for quite the story!

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: I didn't think we'd be able to climb all the way up here...

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: What a great view! I just wanna shout at the top of my lungs!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah! And even though we might not be viewing the meteor shower from here, it's a good place to practice.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Oops, I was having too much fun and almost forgot about that.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Before I left Inazuma, many people heard that I was looking for a meteor shower, so they told me that they wanted to make wishes.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: I told them that they could write their wishes down on paper, so I ended up collecting several dozens of wishes...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Woah, that many!?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So you want to help convey all those wishes?

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: That's part of it, but more importantly, I've been wondering why people link meteor showers and wishes in the first place.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: After a lot of thought, I think I've figured it out.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: People use fireworks to remember their most precious memories, and these memories sparkle and shine each time the fireworks fly.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: In other words, fireworks symbolize the past.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: And shooting stars make people think of wishes because wishes carry people's brilliant hopes and expectations for the future.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: One represents the past, and the other the future. They both bloom in the sky, but have completely different meanings behind them.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: It's really beautiful, isn't it?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Very true...

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: It's clear to me that I'm not the only one holding this belief — I'm sure my ancestor had similar views.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: I think that's how he drew inspiration from the meteor shower...

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: His method was a wish of sorts to begin with — to join the past and future together and combine their beauty.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: At first, I wasn't completely serious about using the opportunity to travel abroad to see a meteor shower...

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: But it became something like a mission once everyone had handed their wishes over to me.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yoimiya...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well said! And here Paimon thought you needed practice.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Huh, that was fine? You both understand what I'm trying to say? Honestly, I thought it was pretty messy...

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: I mean, these are all abstract topics that evoke a... sense of admiration that's hard to put into words.

choices.text: Then, have you ever considered that if you can't find it...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #({NICKNAME}...)

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: I did consider that possibility, and I won't lie — it'd be a real bummer if that were the case.

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: I know that's the most realistic conclusion, and it's not like luck has to be on my side.

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: But there's a premise to every legend, and that's belief!

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: If I didn't take this step, it's not like a meteor shower would just rain upon me, either.

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: I wouldn't be where I am now. I wouldn't have known that they respond to wishes, and I wouldn't have seen all these beautiful sights in Sumeru.

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: So I'm looking forward to the rest of our journey — every single step of it.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...You really are amazing, Yoimiya.

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: Eh, what?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, nothing. Paimon just thinks you're doing a good job with the wishes. Now we just need one other thing.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Like we said earlier, we're going to need to build a device.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: We'll need to look for the purest ore in Sumeru.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yep, and once we use it to create an observation device, we can find where the meteor shower will be.

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: I see. The purest ore...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: We can go somewhere else to look for it.

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: Hmm... Then, why don't we go back to Sumeru City and ask the blacksmith?

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: I chatted with him a bit when Avin was showing me around. He seems really knowledgeable. I bet he'll know something.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh... But wouldn't we be bothering him?

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: No one knows more about ore than a blacksmith!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's true...

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: Let's go! Hehe, I wish we could fly over!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What are we gonna do? If we really ask the blacksmith, he's gonna give us funny looks for sure!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: We'll just have to roll with the punches...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: *sigh* You're right. Paimon will do her best to not say anything wrong!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: At first, Paimon felt bad about keeping Yoimiya in the dark...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But now, it feels like we made the right decision.

choices.text: I want her to see that meteor shower.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yup, that's why we're doing all this!

choices.text: I want her to have her cake and eat it, too.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You briefly explain the purpose of your visit to the blacksmith.

dialogues.speaker: Ahangar
dialogues.text: You want to use the purest material to create a star observation device? Hmm... A pair of specially crafted lenses should do the job.

dialogues.speaker: Ahangar
dialogues.text: However, "purest material" is too vague. It'd be better if you were more specific...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Do you have any alternatives for us?

dialogues.speaker: Ahangar
dialogues.text: Firstly, this all sounds rather strange. I've never heard that legend about meteor showers. You sure you're not just messing with me?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: (Sorry for the trouble, but we are kind of messing with someone...)

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Sorry... Inazuma's pretty far, so maybe some key information got lost across the ocean.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Still, I want to at least give it a shot. Even though the information's vague, can you help us at all?

dialogues.speaker: Ahangar
dialogues.text: Well, sure. Why don't I use some materials that might fit the bill, and create up a mock-up device for you?

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: That'd be great. Thanks so much for your help!

dialogues.speaker: Ahangar
dialogues.text: No need to be so polite — you're my customer. Also, this kind of project is a nice change of pace.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Using his well-honed skills, the blacksmith constructs three lenses of different make.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: (Maybe we can just pick a random one. It's not like we're really going to use it, anyway...)

dialogues.speaker: Ahangar
dialogues.text: No, that won't do. I don't think I can justify that to myself...

dialogues.speaker: Ahangar
dialogues.text: If these were for ordinary use, then it'd be acceptable... barely. But if you want a product that is top-notch, this is far from ideal.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: (Gah, why are you so interested all of a sudden?)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Then what do we do...?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, what now...?

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Don't worry too much about the material. If you think it'll be difficult to obtain, we can get it for you.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: I want to try all our options.

dialogues.speaker: Ahangar
dialogues.text: Hmm...

dialogues.speaker: Ahangar
dialogues.text: Since we're on the topic of legends, allow me to tell you one about blacksmiths.

dialogues.speaker: Ahangar
dialogues.text: All of us in Sumeru know about this legendary forging material. It possesses excellent properties that are matched by no other...

dialogues.speaker: Ahangar
dialogues.text: Using it to forge something is every blacksmith's dream.

dialogues.speaker: Ahangar
dialogues.text: Some spend their entire lives searching for this material in vain, while others have it in their possession, yet never use it in their forge.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Why's that?

dialogues.speaker: Ahangar
dialogues.text: That's because the material is too precious. Many believe themselves unworthy to work with it due to a lack of skill.

dialogues.speaker: Ahangar
dialogues.text: In other words, not only does it represent the pinnacle of material quality, but also the culmination of a smith's skills.

dialogues.speaker: Ahangar
dialogues.text: I constantly practice and hone myself so when I do encounter this material, we won't pass each other by like two ships in the night.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: So you mean that it symbolizes dreams?

dialogues.speaker: Ahangar
dialogues.text: Dreams, inspiration, obsession, focus... Call it what you want. But if you take it to symbolize "purity," then I believe it is your goal as well.

dialogues.speaker: Ahangar
dialogues.text: We call it Urstone, but in truth, neither I nor my colleagues have ever seen it.

dialogues.speaker: Ahangar
dialogues.text: It's more like a goal, and also a warning.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: This fits perfectly with the tale of the meteor shower.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Then why don't we go looking for it?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Is it even something we can find?

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: Exactly! We're chasing down a legend, after all. What's true or not doesn't matter as much.

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: If we do find it, that's a big win for us! And if we don't, maybe we can still find something that could be used as a substitute.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: When you put it like that...

response.speaker: Farid
response.text: Excuse me. If I might intrude, have you seen a child in a wheelchair?

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: Yeah, she and I were hanging out not that long ago. What's the matter?

response.speaker: Niousha
response.text: Do you know where she went? She hasn't returned home yet...

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: Huh? I wonder why? When we split up, she said she was heading home.

response.speaker: Niousha
response.text: Oh dear... *sigh*

response.speaker: Niousha
response.text: I'm sorry if I seemed worked up. I'm Avin's mother.

response.speaker: Niousha
response.text: She's been depressed ever since she fell ill and was forced to use a wheelchair. I'm concerned about her mental health.

response.speaker: Niousha
response.text: If she does something reckless because she's not in a good state of mind...

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: It's okay, don't worry. We'll help you find her.

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: I can't say that I know her very well, but I think she just has a lot on her mind, and is trying to come to terms with her feelings.

response.speaker: Niousha
response.text: That's reassuring... *sigh* She doesn't want to tell me anything, probably because she thinks nothing she says would make either of us feel better.

response.speaker: Niousha
response.text: But I can't tell what she's thinking if we don't communicate...

response.speaker: Niousha
response.text: I'm worried that I'll panic and make things worse by saying the wrong thing.

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: Don't worry, I'm sure she has a reason for wanting some space to herself at the moment. We should just be open and understanding with her.

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: But that does bring me to a question I've been mulling over in my head... Do you think there's something else going on in her life?

response.speaker: Niousha
response.text: Not that I'm aware of, I just know the illness was a big blow to her...

response.speaker: Niousha
response.text: She's always been physically active. She absolutely loved to run and jump, and she told me that she wanted to become a great adventurer some day.

response.speaker: Niousha
response.text: But after she became ill, she lost strength in both legs. She hasn't been able to stand since.

response.speaker: Niousha
response.text: We've consulted with countless doctors, but they're all stumped. They said all she can do is slowly recuperate. No one can say for sure if she'll ever stand or walk again.

response.speaker: Niousha
response.text: She believes that her legs will never recover, and her dreams of seeing the world would be forever shattered. *sigh* It's... This was all too sudden, too unfair.

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: Okay, I understand. I'll find a way to bring her around.

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: Sorry, but it looks like we'll have to put our meteor shower search on hold.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Of course. Avin's safety is more important.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We're coming with you!

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: Mister Blacksmith, do you remember seeing a child in a wheelchair?

response.speaker: Ahangar
response.text: Sorry, afraid not. I've been keeping my eyes on my anvil.

response.speaker: Ahangar
response.text: But you're looking for someone... I suggest dropping in on Sadegh.

response.speaker: Ahangar
response.text: He's my supplier. If anyone's aware of the comings and goings in Treasures Street, it'd be him.

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: Do you know where we can find him?

response.speaker: Ahangar
response.text: He's probably resting just over there. It's not far.

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: Got it. Thanks for your help with everything!

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: We'll go over there and see what we can find out. Don't worry, I don't think she's gone too far.

response.speaker: Niousha
response.text: Thank you so much. He and I will continue asking around in the city.

response.speaker: Niousha
response.text: If you find her, please let me know... Thanks again for helping.

choices.text: Treat it as a fun excursion.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Excuse me, have you seen a child in a wheelchair?

dialogues.speaker: Sadegh
dialogues.text: Hmm, now that you mention it, that does ring a bell. I was moving some boxes at the time, and I saw her pushing her wheelchair so hard she was panting.

dialogues.speaker: Sadegh
dialogues.text: I asked if she needed help, but she didn't respond, as if she didn't hear me.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Sounds like there really was something on her mind.

dialogues.speaker: Sadegh
dialogues.text: Yeah, that was the impression I got, too. What's wrong? Did she go missing?

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Yes, so we're looking for her.

dialogues.speaker: Sadegh
dialogues.text: I see... That's rather worrying. I know — I'll ask my friends and see if they know anything.

dialogues.speaker: Sadegh
dialogues.text: She went that way. If you ask people as you go, hopefully you'll track her down.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Okay, thanks! If you find out anything, don't forget to tell the people with the green scarves!

dialogues.speaker: Sadegh
dialogues.text: Haha, you mean the Corps of Thirty? Don't worry, I got it.

talks.objective: Look for Avin and ask about her whereabouts

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Excuse me! We're looking for a child in a wheelchair...

dialogues.speaker: Nidal
dialogues.text: Oh, I remember her. She went that way not too long ago.

dialogues.speaker: Nidal
dialogues.text: I asked her what she was doing — it's my job, after all. She just said she had something important to do and didn't want to be disturbed.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That seems a little weird.

dialogues.speaker: Nidal
dialogues.text: Whatever the case, she left the city. If you follow that road, you should be able to find her.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Gotcha. Thanks a lot!

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Hello there! Did a child in a wheelchair pass this way?

dialogues.speaker: Jahan
dialogues.text: A wheelchair? Oh, so that's what it was...

dialogues.speaker: Jahan
dialogues.text: I didn't get a good look, but something going pretty fast went sliding down that slope over there.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Oh no, how dangerous.

dialogues.speaker: Jahan
dialogues.text: For sure. There's terrain of all sorts outside the city, and if that was the kid...

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Got it. It was over there, right? We'll be going now. Thanks!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey! Are you alright?

dialogues.speaker: Avin
dialogues.text: I fell off my wheelchair...

dialogues.speaker: Avin
dialogues.text: I can't move around without it... Why...? Why!?

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: It's okay, you're okay, you're not hurt.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: I'll take care of her. Can you two look for her wheelchair?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: No problem! We'll be right back!

talks.objective: Investigate the traces on the ground

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (After Avin fell off, the wheelchair would've kept going. It should be somewhere up ahead.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (It must've slowed down. Can't be far now.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Those aren't wheelchair tracks. Let's look somewhere else.)

talks.objective: Investigate the traces on the ground
Defeat all opponents and recover the wheelchair

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You return the wheelchair to Avin.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Alright, we're in luck. Looks like the wheelchair's still working.

dialogues.speaker: Avin
dialogues.text: That's good... *sigh* Or else my family would have to pay for another one.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: You feeling any better? I know that must've been really scary for you.

dialogues.speaker: Avin
dialogues.text: Mm...

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: It's alright, you're safe now. We'll bring you back.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Do you feel okay telling me why you had to come here, despite the risks?

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: If you don't want anyone else to know, we'll definitely keep it a secret!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's right! You can trust us.

dialogues.speaker: Avin
dialogues.text: The Aranara Carving...

dialogues.speaker: Avin
dialogues.text: My bestest friend... He went missing...

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: The carving? You mean the one I gave you?

dialogues.speaker: Avin
dialogues.text: Yeah. My illness is really bad. It's not just my legs — I've forgotten a lot of stuff, too.

dialogues.speaker: Avin
dialogues.text: I used to love running. I loved the feeling it gave me, and the sound of wind rushing by my ears.

dialogues.speaker: Avin
dialogues.text: But the longer I sit, the cloudier those memories get. I'm starting to forget how it feels to "love" something.

dialogues.speaker: Avin
dialogues.text: But when I saw that wood carving, I remembered that I once had a best friend. He'd always run with me.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, was he an Aranara!?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Um, Paimon meant that it couldn't have been an Aranara, right? They're just fairy tale characters!

dialogues.speaker: Avin
dialogues.text: But they aren't! They're real! They couldn't be more real!

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Hey, I understand. Okay, let's calm down. Tell us what happened so we can help you.

dialogues.speaker: Avin
dialogues.text: Sorry, I got carried away... and I don't have any evidence to show you...

dialogues.speaker: Avin
dialogues.text: Everyone says you can't see Aranara anymore once you become an adult. You have to say goodbye to your Aranara friends forever.

dialogues.speaker: Avin
dialogues.text: I can't remember his name or how he looked like... and soon, I'll even forget that he used to run with me...

dialogues.speaker: Avin
dialogues.text: I don't want to become an adult... Not like this.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: I understand now... When you saw that carving, you were reminded of your friend.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: You came out here to look for him and remember that friendship, no matter how difficult things got. Isn't that right?

dialogues.speaker: Avin
dialogues.text: Yes. I want to see him. I want to tell him that I'm not angry with him, and that I didn't want to break our promise. But then... this happened.

dialogues.speaker: Avin
dialogues.text: I'm not angry with him, not at all.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Cheer up — something beautiful has happened.

dialogues.speaker: Avin
dialogues.text: Beautiful?

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: That's right. You remembered something about the Aranara, haven't you?

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Once you start remembering more things, you'll be able to find your friend again.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: And I'll help you!

dialogues.speaker: Avin
dialogues.text: Yoimiya...

dialogues.speaker: Avin
dialogues.text: Does this mean that you can also see Aranara?

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Sorry, I don't know if I can. I've only just arrived in Sumeru. Maybe I haven't seen one yet, or maybe I can't see them at all.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: But that doesn't matter. Whether I can see them or not doesn't change my belief that you can.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What do we do?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon really wants to help her. She didn't deserve any of this — not her illness, or being separated from her friend. But...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Yoimiya, can we talk?

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: Huh, me? Sure. Um, sorry, wait here for a moment. We'll be right back.

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: What's wrong? You look so serious all of a sudden.

choices.text: Do you really believe in the Aranara?

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: Oh, did you think I was over-promising back there? Don't worry, I have experience with this kind of thing.

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: To her, reuniting with her Aranara friend is the "result." But recapturing her past joy and belief in herself is the "process," and that's where our help is needed.

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: I'm guessing that her sudden illness made her feel like she may not be able to realize her dreams anymore. It also made it difficult for her to hold onto the happy memories and dreams she had.

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: Everyone has their own imagination. After some chance coincidence, she met an "Aranara."

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: So as long as we help her rediscover that same feeling she once had, her "Aranara" will return naturally.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, so that's what you're thinking...

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: Adults only want to believe in objective reality. In doing so, they may unintentionally do harm to the innocent fantasies of children.

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: But I think there are ways to get even subjective things back.

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: So how about it? Wanna help me out?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hehe, looks like all this excitement made you forget your original goal again.

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: *sigh* If we didn't do anything to help, I wouldn't be able to watch a meteor shower, even if it appeared right now.

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: And would the stars really want their caller to have such a heartless soul?

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: What are you trying to say?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Because we can actually summon the Aranara.

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: R—Really?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Just watch. We have some tricks up our sleeves!

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: You blow the leaf to call forth the Aranara...

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: Whoa... So this is an Aranara...

response.speaker: Arapurva
response.text: Very unexpected. The Lord of Dendro did not say that there would be strange Nara.

response.speaker: Arapurva
response.text: Aranara trust Golden Nara. If that were not so... I would not have appeared.

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: I'm the one who should be apologizing! Sorry, let me explain.

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: I know that you only want to be seen by people you trust. It's rash of me to butt in...

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: But this girl once had an Aranara as her best friend, and they haven't met in a very long time.

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: She's been quite ill, and her world has turned upside down. It's been so long since she's been able to see her friend that even her memory of him has become hazy...

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: Parting with a friend like that is too sad, and she never wanted that to happen.

response.speaker: Arapurva
response.text: I remember Nara Avin and Arashani.

response.speaker: Arapurva
response.text: All Nara grow up, and when they do, they will say goodbye to their young selves.

response.speaker: Arapurva
response.text: All Nara want to prepare for that, but the truth is... very few succeed.

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: That's why I want to help her. Her world is still very small — too small for all the sadness she has to bear.

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: As things are, all she can do is sit alone and think about how happiness is leaving her little by little, about how life has been so unfair to her...

response.speaker: Arapurva
response.text: I understand. Her world is very small, so disappointment is very large.

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: Yes. Maybe we're already used to bad luck, and we know how to deal with feelings of sorrow and disappointment.

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: But this is her first time dealing with any of this. Life can trip anyone up. What's most important in times like this...

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: Is for us to support one another.

response.speaker: Arapurva
response.text: Hmm...

response.speaker: Arapurva
response.text: It seems that Red Nara has not yet grown up.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Eh? What do you mean by that?

response.speaker: Arapurva
response.text: Time is very important to Nara. Nara walk with time. They remember much, and they forget much.

response.speaker: Arapurva
response.text: But Red Nara is different. You know how young Nara think. The warmth in your heart is very pure, and it is fierce like the sun.

response.speaker: Arapurva
response.text: I believe you are a trustworthy Nara.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So, that means...

response.speaker: Arapurva
response.text: I can bring you all to see Arashani.

response.speaker: Avin
response.text: Eh? Th—Thank you...

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: Thanks for trusting us!

response.speaker: Arapurva
response.text: Arashani is in Mawtiyima Forest. But Nara Avin might not be able to see Arashani unless she is prepared.

response.speaker: Arapurva
response.text: It is not very complicated or difficult, though. Let me lead the way.

choices.text: Don't worry, I don't doubt your reasoning, it's just...
How do you plan to help her?

talks.objective: Go to the Mawtiyima Forest with Arapurva

dialogues.speaker: Nidal
dialogues.text: If that's all, then, I'll be continuing my patrol.

dialogues.speaker: Gurgen
dialogues.text: Mm, sorry, I'm not sure. I've been tending to the herbs.

dialogues.speaker: Salar
dialogues.text: A child in a wheelchair? Sorry, I didn't see anyone like that. I was organizing some things.

dialogues.speaker: Nevida
dialogues.text: I'm very sorry, but I haven't seen this child. I've been settling disputes all day.

dialogues.speaker: Nevida
dialogues.text: If they have suffered an accident, please send them to Bimarstan immediately. I can help you make arrangements.

dialogues.speaker: Ahangar
dialogues.text: I'll keep an eye out for you. If I see her, I'll try to keep her here with me.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: #I was wondering... have you seen your {M#sister}{F#brother} yet?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Yup, but {M#she}{F#he} said that {M#she}{F#he}'d meet us at the end of our journey — and then {M#she}{F#he} left.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: #I see. It seems {M#she}{F#he} has {M#her}{F#his} own things to worry about...

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: #But it's alright. At least you were able to talk. How did {M#she}{F#he} look? Was {M#she}{F#he} doing well? Had {M#she}{F#he} changed in any way?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Well, according to {M#him}{F#her}, nothing's really changed. {M#He}{F#She}'s hanging in there.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Hehe, that sure is reassuring!

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: I believe that you two will come to an understanding once your journey is over.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: You are siblings, after all.

dialogues.speaker: Ahangar
dialogues.text: (Kids these days... Her friends sure seem worried.)

dialogues.speaker: Sadegh
dialogues.text: (I've got two more vendors to visit... Ah well, there's no rush. I'm going to take a break.)

dialogues.speaker: Nidal
dialogues.text: (I suppose this is part of what the Mahamata calls our "duties.")

dialogues.speaker: Jahan
dialogues.text: (No one was accompanying that kid...?)

dialogues.speaker: Salar
dialogues.text: (Let's check how much fertilizer we have left again...)

dialogues.speaker: Gurgen
dialogues.text: (Will this amount of water do?)

dialogues.speaker: Nevida
dialogues.text: (Settling disputes is exhausting...)

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: (I have to calm her down first.)

dialogues.speaker: Avin
dialogues.text: (Why... Why did this happen to me...)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Look, it's the wheelchair! So the hilichurls took it!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We gotta get it back before they damage it!
